raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I've been farming these 10.1 mu for a long time now — my wife and I, we know every piece of this land. Some of it's better suited for cotton, the rest I do the wheat-maize rotation like most folks around here.

Let me lay out the year.

---

**Wheat — about 7 mu**

I already planted the wheat back in October, so that's done. Right now it's coming out of winter and greening up. What I'm deciding now is how to manage it through to harvest in June.

I put down about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting (15-15-15 type), which is maybe 4 kg of N before winter. Now at jointing I'll topdress urea — about 20 kg urea per mu, that's roughly 9 kg N. So total N comes to around 13 kg/mu. The extension guy last year said I could go to 15 or 16, but honestly, urea's not cheap and my wheat usually hits around 450 kg/mu anyway. I'd rather save the money.

Irrigation — I'll water at greenup (already did once), then at jointing with the topdress, and one more at flowering if it doesn't rain. That's 3 times, maybe 4 if it's dry. The electric pump is metered so every watering costs me, but you can't skip flowering water, the grain won't fill.

For weeds I'll spray a herbicide once in spring — nothing fancy, whatever the agri-store has. No insects usually bad enough to spray for.

**Maize — same 7 mu, after wheat**

The window is tight — after I combine the wheat in early June, I've got maybe 3-4 days to get the maize in. I use no-till direct seeding with a rented planter, my neighbor runs one. It's how we all do it now; the old way of plowing between crops doesn't work, not enough time.

I'll buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan or Xianyu type, whatever the shop has fresh. About 4 kg/mu, costs maybe 50 yuan/mu. Fertilizer at planting: compound again, about 30 kg/mu of 20-10-10, and then topdress urea at big-flare stage (around V8-V10), maybe 15 kg urea. Total N about 15 kg/mu for maize.

Irrigation — summer rain usually covers most of it, but if July turns dry I'll pump once or twice. Expect around 500 kg/mu if the weather behaves.

Pest-wise, corn borer and fall armyworm — I'll spray once at whorl stage, that's usually enough.

**Cotton — 3.1 mu**

The cotton plot is on the sandier ground where the wheat doesn't do as well. Cotton prices have been decent, and I've always kept some cotton going — my father grew it, I grew up picking it.

I'll plant mid-late April, probably this week or next when the soil warms up. Using hybrid seed, Bt type, about 1.5 kg/mu. Before planting I'll put down compound fertilizer around 25 kg/mu, then topdress at budding and again at flowering with urea.

Cotton takes more watching than wheat or maize — aphids, bollworm (even with Bt you still get some), and mite problems. I'll probably spray 4-5 times through the season. That costs money but you can't let the bollworm in.

Picking is the hardest part. With just me and my wife, 3 mu of cotton takes us weeks of bending over. I'll hire one or two women from the village for 3-4 days in peak picking, pay them by the kilo picked.

**Labor and money**

My son works in the city, sends some money home but can't help in the fields. My wife and I do almost everything ourselves, hire the planter and combine for wheat and maize, and the pickers for cotton.

Total input cost I'm figuring maybe 4,800 to 5,000 yuan for the whole farm. That's seed, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation electricity, and custom machine hire. Hired labor for cotton another 600-800 yuan. It's a lot of cash up front, especially the fertilizer in spring — I'll pay the shop and settle at harvest if I need to.
